rationale: TF-wide knockout library (7,294 guides, 96 non-targeting) in human small-intestinal organoids with a CHGA-iRFP enteroendocrine (EEC) reporter and a MUC2-mNeonGreen goblet reporter; differentiated organoids were sorted into iRFP+ (EEC), mNeonGreen+ and double-negative fractions in two biological replicates. The fractions of one replicate come from one transduced culture (they correlate more with each other than with the other replicate), so replicate is a blocking term (1 residual df). Repressors of EEC fate such as ZNF800 should be enriched in iRFP+ versus double-negative cells; genes required for EEC fate (NEUROG3) depleted. Counts are the 11 per-sample GEO files merged by guide; depth is low (~300 reads per guide). Composition: in the double-negative fraction the top 1% of guides hold 56-59% of reads (IRF2 and NFKB1 guides alone take ~30%; 29-33% in iRFP+), so non-targeting guides make up 0.7% of negative-fraction reads versus 1.3% of iRFP+ reads. With library totals 65% of control guides reached p < 0.05 and 640 of 642 calls were enriched, an artifact of the shift. The primary analysis therefore normalizes to the 96 non-targeting guides (totals = control); a median-ratio run is kept as a sensitivity check.
